correspondence.component_scope: southern opening and required northward connection
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in flat vegetated lowland east of agricultural clearings. The selected westward/northwestward turn and subsequent northgoing interval were inspected in both originals. Patchy cloud/shadow and indistinct low-relief cover leave the required continuous receiving corridor unresolved. No spring, natural source or precise river course is inferred. The uncertainty is which northgoing collector/receiving depression this southern starting area enters, not exact bank alignment or whether water is currently present.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper agricultural receiving corridor
correspondence.finding: North of the unresolved interval, the selection occupies the connected darker vegetated lowland among agricultural fields. Its northwestward approach and northeastward return remain in the same broad receiving corridor; surrounding field drainage is not individually named.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle corridor and marsh approach
correspondence.finding: The route continues northward along the agricultural margin into wider marshy ground, with a westward bend before returning north. Visible connected wetland/vegetation corridors support the ordinary joins between these stored parts. No hydronym boundary is inferred from their divisions.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: broad middle wetland and foot of hills
correspondence.finding: The selection turns northeast through the broad shallow-water and marsh complex, then northwest toward the western foot of the isolated wooded hills. Surrounding wetland arms and patches of open water form a connected receiving landscape. The study’s Puente Largo/La Yana descriptions supply bounded managed-water context, without assigning all wetland surfaces one lake or river name.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower northgoing wetland corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected northgoing interval and northeastward continuation occupy the wetland east of the larger western lagoon, then approach the coastal estuarine network. The continuous wetland setting supports ordinary passage without requiring a single presently wet thread. The separate managed La Redonda–La Leche transfer is not substituted for this selected corridor, and Canal La Yana is not automatically extended across every part.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal estuarine route and separate endings
correspondence.finding: The last stored part continues along the coastal marsh/estuarine receiving corridor, through the crossing setting at the shoreward margin, toward shallow marine water. Original coastal pixels expose both the channel approach and its receiving shore. The source ending is shore-adjacent in the estuarine/coastal transition; the rendered ending lies farther seaward in shallow open marine water. Neither is promoted to an exact current outlet or bank vertex.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices within the selected fragment.

findings.material_gap: The selected southern opening and the required northwest-to-north connection across the flat vegetated/agricultural plain, spanning original parts0–2, are not established at useful ordinary corridor scale. The overview and one enlarged original show the setting, but patchy cloud/shadow and undifferentiated low-relief cover do not expose a definite continuous receiving corridor for that interval. Basin-level prose and the study’s small regional diagram cannot close this specific link. This is not a demand for exact banks or continuously wet water. Specifically, the images do not distinguish which northgoing lowland/collector receives the selected southern starting area through the intervening cloudy and cultivated terrain. They show a broad plain, but not an identifiable common receiving depression for this required transfer. A proven common lowland with only an invisible narrow channel would have been sufficient; that positive receiving relationship is what remains missing.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen eastern ice opening and westward glacial passage
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening lies within a continuous mapped glacier trough. The selection runs west around the northern mountain ridges, enters the broader ice field associated with the Bering Glacier label and turns south along the western side of the interior rock ridges. Its ordinary ice-field geography is covered. The mapped modeled line is not interpreted as a named river or an observed on-ice/subglacial watercourse.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southward ice turn and southern margin
correspondence.finding: The selection turns southeast across the mapped ice field toward its southern margin, beside several distinct unnamed marginal lakes. The complete glaciated setting and approach to the selected small southern lake are depicted; neighboring lakes are not all treated as selected through-waters.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: small southern lake to feeder transfer
correspondence.finding: The selected part leaves the small southern ice-margin lake and descends toward a separately mapped tributary below. The detailed National Map original depicts the lake, intervening rock/snow-covered slope and the lower feeder without establishing their through-transfer. The independent narrow image shows lakes, snow-covered relief and the receiving slope but does not resolve the ordinary outlet connection. Proximity and modeled continuity alone are insufficient. This is the single material correspondence gap.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: western feeder and duktoth receiving join
correspondence.finding: Below the unresolved lake transfer, a mapped west-to-east tributary valley runs into the broad Duktoth River receiving water. The selected corridor follows this ordinary tributary setting and reaches its junction with the main Duktoth valley. The generalized route is not forced onto a precise bank or every small tributary curve.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle duktoth valley
correspondence.finding: The selection turns south then southwest through the broad water corridor repeatedly labeled Duktoth River, between the surrounding mountain fronts. Side-stream and outwash joins are depicted, including the broader eastern receiving fans and the western Hope Creek neighborhood. The mapped river continues through one valley to the lower coastal plain.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower duktoth and coastal branch receivers
correspondence.finding: The lower selected Duktoth corridor bends southeast and east through the wet coastal plain. The original depicts the adjoining tributary/fan network and the North Channel Yakataga River joining the Duktoth receiving setting. The South Channel Yakataga River remains a distinct neighboring course. The selected stage3 fragment reaches the stage2 continuation in the same lower Duktoth corridor.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: actual source and render coastal endings
correspondence.finding: The final stage2 part continues to the Duktoth coastal mouth/bar setting. The retained source endpoint is on the landward beach-bar/shoreline side of the final bend; the rendered endpoint is farther south at the adjacent coastal-water margin. The map shows the river bending west behind the shore barrier and its common Gulf of Alaska receiving setting. Both supplied endpoints are retained separately; neither is moved to the map's western channel opening, and exact current shoreline/tidal alignment is not asserted.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern chosen opening and southwest-running Chrome Creek valley
correspondence.finding: The original shows the opening within the same branching mountain drainage as the directly labeled Chrome Creek. The selected westward opening and southwest descent remain within this continuous creek valley, passing side-stream junctions and reaching the plainly mapped North Fork Smith River join. No intervening lake, glacier, impoundment, separate basin or missing transfer is shown. The first position is not asserted to be the official source or exact legal name boundary; that limited naming uncertainty does not prevent ordinary geographic correspondence.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: North Fork Smith River from Chrome Creek past Baldface and Fall creek joins toward the state boundary
correspondence.finding: The route turns south onto the larger labeled North Fork, follows its eastward bend and continues south past distinct eastern Baldface Creek and Fall Creek mouths. Repeated fork labels and the mapped channel establish the receiving connection. Neither eastern tributary is substituted for the selected opening.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: North Fork through the Oregon–California boundary, Diamond Creek junction and lower canyon to Stony Creek and Gasquet vicinity
correspondence.finding: The inspected channel continues across the state boundary, receives the separately labeled Diamond Creek drainage, passes the Pine Flat Mountain and Still Creek setting, bends around Gasquet Mountain and continues to the Stony Creek join. The selected corridor follows the same connected canyon at ordinary map scale. Stored part boundaries do not indicate separate rivers, and no lake-to-feeder or cross-basin gap is required.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Gasquet-area fork confluence and west/southwest receiving valley alongside Highway 199
correspondence.finding: The lower North Fork meets the separately mapped eastern Middle Fork corridor near Gasquet and Ward Field. The selected path takes the connected westward receiving channel, follows its large southwest bends beside Highway 199 and reaches the major southeastern tributary join near South Fork Road. The map establishes the joins and the continuing main-river valley. A precise legal vertex where every fork label ends is not inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Main Smith River westward and northward bends into the coastal plain
correspondence.finding: Below the major southeastern join the source directly labels Smith River. The selected river passes the Mill Creek and Clarks Creek joining setting, bends north past the Peacock Creek and Sultan Creek area and continues toward the Little Mill Creek and Rowdy Creek receiving corridor. The broad river remains continuous across both narrow valley and coastal-plain sections. Nearby lakes, drainage ditches and sloughs are not adopted as alternative selected routes.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Smith River bend, estuary and separate actual endings
correspondence.finding: The stage 2 fragment continues the same lower Smith River through the Rowdy Creek joining area and the westward bend, then turns north into its elongated coastal estuary. The retained source ending is in the mapped inner estuarine/channel setting. The rendered ending is farther west at the ocean-side coastal margin next to that estuary. Both belong to the same ordinary coastal receiving setting; they are not asserted to coincide with the actual outlet throat. The map depicts the estuary continuing north beyond the ending area. The generalized rendered extension is not evidence of an exact channel through the coastal spit, a navigation route or the current shoreline.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based original stored-part indices, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen northern glacier opening
correspondence.finding: The northern selected opening lies in a glaciated valley between exposed mountain ridges. The route runs southeast through the mapped ice corridor to the eastern bend. Both the opening and continuous passage are depicted; no natural-river label or precise on-ice/subglacial hydraulic route is assigned.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern ice margin and southwest glacial turn
correspondence.finding: The selection turns south along the eastern side of the broad ice field, then southwest and west through the continuous glaciated terrain toward the lake margin. The Yakutat Glacier label lies on the contiguous regional ice field to the west; nearby separate rock spurs and glacier arms are retained as distinct surroundings. No precise internal glacier-name boundary is claimed.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern harlequin lake entry and fragment join
correspondence.finding: The selected ice corridor meets the eastern lake-margin/foreland setting and enters the connected water of Harlequin Lake. Mapped outwash braids and the lake margin provide an ordinary continuous receiving setting; exact present ice-front location is not needed. The end of the stage3 fragment and start of stage2 lie within the same lake interior.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: through harlequin lake
correspondence.finding: The stage2 selection crosses the connected Harlequin Lake basin southwest toward its western outlet. Harlequin Lake is directly labeled. A Dangerous River cartographic label also spans part of the lake interior, but this is not evidence that the lake or selected upper ice field is one natural river.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: western lake outlet and first river bends
correspondence.finding: The mapped western outlet directly connects Harlequin Lake to the meandering Dangerous River corridor. The selected line passes through the outlet and follows the first bends across the low coastal plain. The nearby Miller Creek and other northern watercourses are separate components, not aliases.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower dangerous river coastal plain
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the broad, repeatedly labeled Dangerous River west-southwest through its braided and meandering coastal-plain belt. Adjacent wetlands and the neighboring Ahrnklin River remain distinct. The final selected river reaches the mapped coastal mouth setting.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: separate source and render coastal endings
correspondence.finding: The source endpoint is retained at the seaward mouth side of the lower river. The rendered endpoint lies farther south beside the adjacent coastal bar/shoreline setting, reached by the supplied final segment. The complete lower original depicts both locations and the common coastal receiving water. The different source/render placements are described separately without changing the geometry or claiming exact current bank, tidal edge or active mouth position.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Inclusive one-based original stored-part span, restarting within each identified fragment.
